title: Getting started with validatoR
text: validate_prediction() compares two numeric vectors length order: first prediction belongs first target, . accuracy valid target pre-corrected phenotype used evaluation produced predictions. 0.52, value simulated. h2 heritability validation population. selection lower base population, base-population value underestimates accuracy. Estimates phenotypes, including slope, also sensitive errors heritability pre-correction fixed effects (Legarra Reverter, 2018). mse rmse meaningful prediction target scale, example partial whole EBV, EBVs true breeding values. var_a, rmse_in_GSD gives RMSE genetic standard deviations. function also takes bootstrap = TRUE plot = TRUE, draws target prediction:  validate_lr(), plot_subgroups = TRUE colours points group. group vector one label per animal, order data. statistics change.
code: res_pred <- validate_prediction(   prediction = toy_validation$partial,   target = toy_validation$pheno,   h2 = 0.3 ) res_pred$stats #>                 value #> n                2000 #> correlation    0.2846 #> slope             0.9 #> intercept       -0.75 #> mean_diff        0.75 #> mse             920.1 #> rmse            30.33 #> accuracy       0.5196 res_rmse <- validate_prediction(   prediction = toy_validation$partial,   target = toy_validation$whole,   var_a = 300,   plot = TRUE ) res_rmse$stats #>                 value #> n                2000 #> correlation      0.85 #> slope             0.9 #> intercept       -0.75 #> mean_diff        0.75 #> mse             32.66 #> rmse            5.715 #> rmse_in_GSD    0.3299 res_rmse$plot res_pred_group <- validate_prediction(   prediction = toy_validation$partial,   target = toy_validation$pheno,   h2 = 0.3,   group = toy_validation$group,   plot = TRUE,   plot_subgroups = TRUE ) res_pred_group$plot

title: Validate predictions with the LR method — validate_lr
text: list two elements, stats plot. stats data frame one row per statistic column value. bootstrap = TRUE also column SE, bootstrap standard error. keeps full precision prints significant digits (see print.validatoR_stats()). rows , p partial w whole EBVs validation animals: n: number validation animals. level_bias: mean(p) - mean(w). 0 means level bias. level_bias_in_GSD: level_bias / sqrt(var_a). var_a provided. dispersion_bias: cov(p, w) / var(p), regression w p. 1 means dispersion bias, values 1 mean partial EBVs -dispersed, values 1 mean -dispersed. accuracy_partial: sqrt(cov(p, w) / ((1 - F) * var_a)), F average inbreeding validation animals. var_a average_inbreeding inbreeding provided. NaN, warning, cov(p, w) negative average inbreeding 1 . average_inbreeding var_a: values used accuracy_partial, returned tables several groups can compared. rho: cor(p, w), ratio accuracies partial whole EBVs. inc_acc: 1 / rho, increase accuracy obtained whole evaluation, ratio accuracy partial evaluation (see Bonifazi et al., 2022). 1 means gain. increase relative partial evaluation percentage, use (inc_acc - 1) * 100. example, rho 0.80 gives inc_acc 1.25, corresponds increase 25%. plot ggplot object plot = TRUE, NULL otherwise.

title: Validate predictions with the LR method — validate_lr
code: p <- toy_validation[, c("id", "partial")] w <- toy_validation[, c("id", "whole")] inb <- toy_validation[, c("id", "inbreeding")]  # all animals, with the accuracy of the partial EBVs res <- validate_lr(p, w, var_a = 300, inbreeding = inb) res$stats #>                         value #> n                        2000 #> level_bias               0.75 #> level_bias_in_GSD      0.0433 #> dispersion_bias           0.9 #> accuracy_partial        0.562 #> average_inbreeding    0.05001 #> var_a                     300 #> rho                      0.85 #> inc_acc                 1.176  # increase in accuracy relative to the partial evaluation, as a # percentage (equal to 17.6 for this toy data) (res$stats["inc_acc", "value"] - 1) * 100 #> [1] 17.64706  # two cohorts as the validation group, plot coloured by cohort, with the # axes in genetic standard deviations vg <- toy_validation[toy_validation$group %in% c("cohort_1", "cohort_2"),                      c("id", "group")] res_vg <- validate_lr(p, w, val_group = vg, var_a = 300, plot = TRUE,                       plot_subgroups = TRUE, plot_verbose = TRUE,                       plot_in_gsd = TRUE) res_vg$plot   # bootstrap SEs (few resamples, to keep the example fast) validate_lr(p, w, var_a = 300, inbreeding = inb,             bootstrap = TRUE, n_boot = 50)$stats #>                         value        SE #> n                        2000        NA #> level_bias               0.75    0.1237 #> level_bias_in_GSD      0.0433   0.00714 #> dispersion_bias           0.9   0.01374 #> accuracy_partial        0.562    0.0111 #> average_inbreeding    0.05001 0.0002066 #> var_a                     300         0 #> rho                      0.85  0.006383 #> inc_acc                 1.176  0.008878

code: # `pheno` is a pre-corrected phenotype simulated with h2 = 0.3, so passing # `h2` gives the accuracy of the partial EBVs (0.52 for this toy data) res <- validate_prediction(   toy_validation$partial,   toy_validation$pheno,   h2 = 0.3 ) res$stats #>                 value #> n                2000 #> correlation    0.2846 #> slope             0.9 #> intercept       -0.75 #> mean_diff        0.75 #> mse             920.1 #> rmse            30.33 #> accuracy       0.5196  # without `h2` (e.g. when comparing against another EBV such as `whole`) no # accuracy is returned; `var_a` adds the RMSE in genetic standard deviations validate_prediction(   toy_validation$partial,   toy_validation$whole,   var_a = 300 )$stats #>                 value #> n                2000 #> correlation      0.85 #> slope             0.9 #> intercept       -0.75 #> mean_diff        0.75 #> mse             32.66 #> rmse            5.715 #> rmse_in_GSD    0.3299  # bootstrap standard errors (few resamples, to keep the example fast) validate_prediction(   toy_validation$partial,   toy_validation$pheno,   h2 = 0.3,   bootstrap = TRUE,   n_boot = 200 )$stats #>                 value       SE #> n                2000       NA #> correlation    0.2846  0.01964 #> slope             0.9  0.06516 #> intercept       -0.75   0.6433 #> mean_diff        0.75   0.6419 #> mse             920.1    28.72 #> rmse            30.33   0.4727 #> accuracy       0.5196  0.03586  # scatter plot of the target on the prediction (grey line: slope 1, # blue line: fitted regression) res_plot <- validate_prediction(   toy_validation$partial,   toy_validation$pheno,   h2 = 0.3,   plot = TRUE ) res_plot$plot   # colour the points by cohort, useful to spot a group that behaves differently validate_prediction(   toy_validation$partial,   toy_validation$pheno,   h2 = 0.3,   group = toy_validation$group,   plot = TRUE,   plot_subgroups = TRUE )$plot
